record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.original_question: A DGLAP next-to-leading-order fit to data with Q^2 > 1 GeV^2 can describe the measurements, but in the low-Q^2 region it implies small-x gluon contributions that become rapidly smaller than the sea-quark contribution at low starting scales. Are such low-Q^2 parton distributions universally valid, and can that universality be tested using low-Q^2 F2^c data?

evidence.quote: Whether such low-Q2 partons are universally valid could be tested using e.g. low-Q2 F2c data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider proton parton distribution functions (PDFs) $f_i(x,Q^2)$ extracted from deep-inelastic scattering structure function data via a next-to-leading-order DGLAP evolution fit restricted to the region $Q^2 > 1\,\text{GeV}^2$. In such fits, the small-$x$ gluon distribution at low starting scales $Q_0^2 \sim 1\,\text{GeV}^2$ is found to become rapidly smaller than the sea-quark distribution as $Q^2$ decreases, and may even turn negative.

(a) Determine whether the parton distributions obtained from such a low-$Q^2$ DGLAP fit are universal, in the sense that the same set of PDFs $\{f_i(x,Q^2)\}$ correctly predicts other inclusive and semi-inclusive observables (in particular structure functions associated with heavy-quark production) in the same low-$Q^2$, small-$x$ kinematic region, via the standard collinear factorization formula
$$F(x,Q^2) = \sum_i \int_x^1 \frac{d\xi}{\xi}\, C_i\!\left(\tfrac{x}{\xi},Q^2\right) f_i(\xi,Q^2),$$
with perturbatively computed coefficient functions $C_i$.

(b) Specifically, formulate and carry out a test of this universality using measurements of the charm contribution $F_2^{c\bar c}(x,Q^2)$ to the proton structure function at low $Q^2$ and small $x$: compare the NLO prediction for $F_2^{c\bar c}$ obtained from the PDFs of the inclusive fit (using e.g. a fixed-flavor-number scheme with charm produced via boson–gluon fusion) with direct measurements of $F_2^{c\bar c}$ in the same kinematic regime, and assess whether the agreement (or lack thereof) supports the universality of the extracted low-$Q^2$ partons.
artifact.category_tag: parton distribution functions and DGLAP evolution
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution was located. Subsequent HERA combined measurements of $F_2^{c\bar c}$ at low $Q^2$ have been used to constrain PDFs and test factorization, but the question of universality of partons extracted from DGLAP fits at very low $Q^2 \sim 1\,\text{GeV}^2$ remains delicate due to the breakdown of fixed-order DGLAP and the need for small-$x$ resummation or dipole-model approaches; no consensus statement of a definitive test outcome was found.
